1. Description

This pairing examines the frequency of coastal flooding at dozens of locations along U.S. coasts. Here, flooding is defined as a day when the water level exceeds a locally defined threshold for “minor flooding.” This feature builds on EPA’s Coastal Flooding indicator and includes the following components:

  • Historical observations since 1950, displayed for selected time intervals.
  • Projected scenarios from 2020 to 2100 for two sea level rise scenarios, displayed for selected time intervals.
